full_name: Stochastic Push--Pull Gradient Tracking on Fixed Exogenous Periodic Directed Networks
source_reference: Feiming Wang, 时变有向网络中随机 Push--Pull 的有效节点数：反例、修正定理与尖锐线性加速判据 (Theorem 7.1)

problem.description: Distributed finite-time nonconvex stochastic optimization for the average objective.

assumptions.name: smoothness_and_lower_gap
assumptions.math: \text{每个 }f_i\text{ 全局 }L\text{-光滑，平均目标 }f\text{ 下有界，且 }0<\Delta:=f(x_0)-\inf f<\infty.

assumptions.name: oracle_unbiased_variance_independence
assumptions.math: \E(\varepsilon_t\mid\cF_{t^-})=0\text{；每个节点的条件二阶矩不超过 }\sigma^2\text{，给定 }\cF_{t^-}\text{ 后同一时刻跨节点条件独立。}

assumptions.name: fixed_exogenous_periodic_network
assumptions.math: \text{存在固定整数 }p\ge1\text{，使 }R_{t+p}=R_t\text{、}C_{t+p}=C_t\text{。矩阵序列在运行前确定并与 oracle 独立。每个 }R_t\text{ 行随机、每个 }C_t\text{ 列随机；二者正对角，每个正权至少为 }a>0\text{，且每个时刻的图强连通。}

output.type: arithmetic average monitored by later theorems; Section 2.1 gives no separate algorithm output rule

main_theorem.rate: 8 sigma sqrt(L Delta / (n_eff T)) plus an instance/network dependent O(1/T) transient.
main_theorem.measure: average expected squared gradient norm at the arithmetic averages

proof.description: Before the theorem, the paper bounds the noise-driven lifted tracker by a finite filter constant V_tau using the noise recursion, column-product contraction, and martingale orthogonality.

The common stepsize ceiling is defined as a minimum containing alpha_st, so every later 0<alpha<=alpha_max also satisfies 0<alpha<=alpha_st; the other terms enforce the hybrid descent condition, eta budget, random feedback budget, and stationary-feedback budget.
proof.produces: positive admissible constant stepsize upper bound alpha_max with alpha_max<=alpha_st

proof.description: Substitute ST into the hybrid-center one-block descent. The state terms in HCLD are grouped through B_k, giving at most (21 alpha/(4H)) sum_k E B_k. The three alpha_max side conditions bound the ST gradient feedback, ST noise feedback, and eta term by alpha H G_K/8, (1/4)Lpq sigma^2 alpha^2 K, and (1/8)Lpq sigma^2 alpha^2 K.
proof.produces: hybrid descent summed with feedback terms absorbed into the left side and noise budget

proof.description: After subtracting 1/8 from the original 5/8 descent coefficient and summing the 5/8, 1/8, and 1/4 noise budgets, telescope the endpoints V_0=f(x_0), V_K>=inf f to obtain the block energy inequality.
Define the shorthand transient coefficient J used in the next division step.
Divide the block-sum inequality by alpha H/2 and use H=ph, so p/H=1/h in the noise term.
proof.produces: bound for block-boundary stationarity sum G_K

proof.description: For a block start s=kp and phase r, use L-smoothness to compare gradients at bar x_{s+r} and bar x_s.
Use Cauchy--Schwarz on the arithmetic average displacement over the r inner steps of the block.
Sum the two within-block comparisons over phases and blocks to convert block-boundary stationarity to all Kp iterates.

For an arbitrary horizon T, choose K=ceil(T/p), N=Kp, extend the same constant-stepsize recursion with 0<alpha<=alpha_max<=alpha_st to the complete final block, drop nonnegative deleted stationarity terms, and define a,b,d from the D-final coefficients.
proof.math: a=\frac{2L^2p^2}{n}\widehat D_g,\quad b=\frac{2L^2p^2}{n}\widehat D_0,\quad d=2L^2p^2\widehat D_\sigma.
proof.produces: complete-block horizon reduction and constants a,b,d

proof.description: Apply the D-final estimate, whose side condition is supplied by 0<alpha<=alpha_max<=alpha_st, to the displacement term in the all-block stationarity bound.
proof.produces: finite-horizon stationarity bound in terms of G_K

proof.description: Substitute the G_K estimate into ST-all and use pK=N to isolate two leading terms and a bracketed O(1/T) remainder.

In the sigma>0 branch choose the horizon-dependent constant stepsize by clipping the balancing value at alpha_max; the proof then denotes the unclipped value by alpha_* and records the two clipping inequalities.
proof.produces: sigma>0 branch: alpha_*:=sqrt(Delta/(Lq sigma^2 T)), 1/alpha_T <= 1/alpha_max + 1/alpha_*, and alpha_T <= alpha_*

proof.description: In the sigma=0 branch choose alpha_T=alpha_max, so all sigma^2 terms in the pre-rate inequality vanish and no balancing parameter alpha_* is used.
proof.produces: sigma=0 branch: alpha_T=alpha_max for the deterministic O(T^{-1}) bound

proof.description: For sigma>0, use the alpha_* clipping inequalities from step 13 and neff=h^2/q to bound the first line of (7.8).
proof.produces: sigma>0 leading 8-sigma term plus clipped-stepsize transient

proof.description: For sigma>0, use the complete-block reduction K=ceil(T/p), N=Kp and the chosen alpha_T to apply the ceiling facts K<=T, N<=pT, N-T<=p-1, making the bracketed noise terms independent of T.
proof.produces: sigma>0 T-independent bounds for the pre-rate bracket

proof.description: In the sigma>0 branch, collect the clipped-leading term and all bounded bracket terms into the explicit finite transient constant printed in (7.11).
proof.produces: sigma>0 finite K_{I,N} independent of T

proof.description: In the sigma=0 branch, substitute alpha_T=alpha_max into (7.8). The leading stochastic term and every sigma^2 bracket term vanish, while the remaining alpha_max, H_0, Delta, a, b, J terms are fixed constants, giving an O(T^{-1}) bound.
proof.ref: Proof of Theorem 7.1, PDF lines 920 and 939

proof.produces: eq:main-upper / (7.3), including T=1, p=1, and sigma=0 boundary cases

key_lemmas.name: PeriodicProductContraction
key_lemmas.role: Provides geometric contraction for column-stochastic zero-sum tracker states and row-stochastic consensus errors.

proof.description: For n>1, every product of n-1 consecutive matrices has every entry at least a^{n-1}; positive diagonal keeps reached nodes and strong connectivity expands a proper reached set by at least one node each step.
proof.produces: uniform positive lower bound for block products

proof.description: Dobrushin decomposition gives l1 contraction by 1-na^{n-1}<=delta on the zero-sum subspace for column-stochastic products; the row-stochastic case applies the same argument to oscillation.
Split an arbitrary long product into complete ell-step blocks and a remainder, then convert l1/oscillation bounds to Euclidean projection bounds.

key_lemmas.name: AverageGainEffectiveNodes
key_lemmas.role: Identifies the average gain h and proves the effective-node inequality used to interpret the final rate.

proof.description: Since each column of C_r-I is zero-sum, Cmix makes the tail of b_r's defining series geometrically summable.
Expand the tracker output o_t=pi_{t+1}^T Y_t over a finite horizon to get the truncated impulse identity.
The geometric tail estimate gives sum_{r<N} ||b_r-b_{r,N}||=O(1); setting every G_r to a fixed W makes Y_t=C_{t-1:0}W converge exponentially to v_t 1^T W.
Along N multiples of p, periodicity and the truncation error identify the same limit as (p^{-1} sum_r b_r^T)W; arbitrary W gives the first two formulas in baverage.
proof.produces: p^{-1} sum_r b_r^T = kappa 1^T and h=n kappa

proof.description: Apply Cauchy--Schwarz to all pn entries of the vectors b_r to get h^2<=nq, with equality iff all entries are equal.

When p=1, the average identity from (4.6) makes the single vector b_0 have all entries equal, so the equality condition in the preceding Cauchy--Schwarz step gives n_eff=n even if the static network is unbalanced.

proof.description: Fix epsilon and define the two-node row-stochastic R_epsilon, Perron vector pi_epsilon, and alternating column-stochastic matrices A_epsilon and B_epsilon.

key_lemmas.name: PredictableFeedbackNonconvergence
key_lemmas.statement_math: \text{存在固定的二节点光滑凸二次实例、固定矩阵集合和一个 horizon-independent 可预测选矩阵规则，使每个 }T\ge3\text{ 与每个常数步长 }\alpha\ge0\text{ 都满足 }\frac1T\sum_{t<T}\E|\nabla f(\bar x_t)|^2\ge\frac{T-2}{64T}.\text{ 因此即使允许主导常数依赖全部固定网络类参数，也不存在 }T^{-1/2}\text{ 收敛界。}
key_lemmas.role: Shows that predictable history-dependent network choice must be excluded from the positive theorem.

proof.description: Choose the two-node quadratic instance, put Rademacher noise only on node one, and define the rank-one matrices J,R^+,R^- with C_t=J.
Define mean/disagreement coordinates and choose R_t=R^+ or R^- according to the pre-sampling sign of d_t; this rule is predictable and all matrices have entries at least 1/4.
With r_t=zeta_t/2, simplify the Push--Pull recursion into scalar recursions for m_t and d_t.
For t>=1 write d_{t+1}=Q_t-alpha r_t with Q_t measurable before r_t; conditioning gives a positive expected absolute disagreement.
For 0<alpha<=1, set q0=1-alpha and expand the expectation recursion for m_t to get a uniform positive mean for t>=2.
Apply Jensen's inequality in the 0<alpha<=1 case to convert the mean lower bound into a second-moment lower bound.
Handle the alpha=0 case separately: the scalar recursion leaves m_t equal to 1.
For alpha>1, the fresh noise in (3.3) gives a conditional variance lower bound larger than 1/4.
Combine the three cases 0<alpha<=1, alpha=0, and alpha>1 for all t>=2, then average over t<T to obtain the theorem conclusion.

key_lemmas.name: PeriodicSpectralDecomposition
key_lemmas.statement_math: \text{设 }A(\alpha)\text{ 在 }|\alpha|<\alpha_1\text{ 上为实解析矩阵族，}A(0)\text{ 有一个简单特征值 }1\text{，并且其余谱包含在 }\{z:|z|\le r_0\}\text{ 中，其中 }r_0<1\text{。则存在 }\alpha_0>0,\ r_0<\theta<1,\ K<\infty\text{，使每个 }|\alpha|\le\alpha_0\text{ 都有分解 }A(\alpha)=\gamma(\alpha)P(\alpha)+F(\alpha),\quad P(\alpha)F(\alpha)=F(\alpha)P(\alpha)=0,\quad \text{其中 }\gamma(\alpha)\text{ 与秩一投影 }P(\alpha)\text{ 均解析，}\gamma(0)=1,\quad \norm{F(\alpha)^j}\le K\theta^j,\quad j\ge0.\quad \text{若 }r_0^{\rm eig},\ell_0^{\rm eig}\text{ 是 }A(0)\text{ 的单位特征值的左右特征向量，并归一化为 }(\ell_0^{\rm eig})^\top r_0^{\rm eig}=1\text{，则 }\gamma'(0)=(\ell_0^{\rm eig})^\top A'(0)r_0^{\rm eig}.
key_lemmas.role: Provides the finite-dimensional analytic slow-stable splitting used in the matching lower-bound proof.

proof.description: Choose disjoint neighborhoods separating the simple unit eigenvalue from the remaining spectrum and fix a positively oriented contour Gamma around 1.
Use compactness and the resolvent identity to shrink alpha_0 so Gamma lies in the resolvent set for all |alpha|<=alpha_0.
The rank of P(alpha) is constant on the connected parameter interval; define gamma and F from the commuting spectral projection to get the decomposition.
After shrinking alpha_0, the spectrum of F(alpha) lies inside |z|<theta_0<theta; Cauchy's matrix formula gives the uniform stable power bound.
Differentiate A(alpha)r(alpha)=gamma(alpha)r(alpha) and multiply by the normalized left eigenvector to obtain the derivative formula.
proof.ref: eq:A.3 and Lemma A.1 proof, PDF lines 1337-1339

key_lemmas.role: Supplies the Appendix A.1 coefficient calculation used by Theorem 3.1 to justify the slow multiplier, slow noise variance, and stable impulse estimate behind (3.2).

proof.description: In reduced coordinates (x_1,x_2,h), w=(h,-h), identify the normalized zeroth-order right and left unit eigenvectors; the nonzero tracker component records the periodic steady tracker response to a consensus gradient.

Set c_A=b_A^T one and c_B=b_B^T one. Starting from the periodic slow state, the zeroth-order primal path has X_t=one u in both phases; differentiating the exact lifted-center recursion at alpha=0 keeps only the zeroth-order X_0 and X_1 terms.

Because nu at alpha=0 is exactly the normalized left coordinate of the slow mode, Lemma A.1 identifies the bracketed first-order coefficient as the eigenvalue derivative; direct substitution into (A.3) gives the same closed form.

Inject a single innovation in phase A or phase B. Its direct contribution to nu_2 is -alpha b_A^T xi_A or -alpha b_B^T xi_B; the induced X perturbation contributes only O(alpha^2) when it re-enters through the following phase gradient.
With iid isotropic noise, square and add the two phase coefficients to obtain the per-period slow noise variance.

Differentiate the left eigenvector equation under the normalization ell(alpha)^T r(alpha)=1 and restrict to the stable complement; multiplying by the stable inverse, whose Neumann series is the future tracker tail, shows that b_A and b_B already include stable resolvent feedback.
proof.produces: phase input derivatives include stable resolvent feedback

proof.description: Define the phase multipliers a_r, within-period products A_r, and the period multiplier Gamma; expand Gamma to first order using the average gain h.

For small positive alpha, Gamma is squeezed between 1-c_2 alpha and 1-c_1 alpha. At block boundaries the comparison process is AR(1) with block martingale difference eta_k; finite phase propagators give the printed block-noise variance.

Use sum_r A_r(alpha)^2=p+O(alpha), 1-Gamma(alpha)^2=2 alpha lambda p h+O(alpha^2), and x_0^2=2 Delta/lambda to simplify the bias term.
The block-boundary variance satisfies a scalar affine recursion; dividing the block-noise variance by 1-Gamma(alpha)^2 gives the periodic steady variance.

If T is not a multiple of p, adding or deleting at most p-1 phases changes the average by O(T^{-1}); combining bias and variance yields (8.7), and under alpha->0 with alpha T->infty the remainder is little-o of the two leading scales.

key_lemmas.statement_math: m_T=\inf_{\alpha\ge0}J_T(\alpha),\qquad \alpha_T^*=\sqrt{\frac{2\Delta}{\lambda\sigma^2qT}},\qquad J_T(\widetilde\alpha_T)\le m_T+T^{-1}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \widetilde\alpha_T\to0,\qquad \widetilde\alpha_TT\to\infty,\qquad s_T=\frac{\Delta}{h\widetilde\alpha_TT}+\frac{\lambda\sigma^2q}{2h}\widetilde\alpha_T,\qquad s_T\ge\sigma\sqrt{\frac{2\lambda\Delta}{\neff T}}.

proof.description: Let m_T be the infimum over all nonnegative stepsizes; substituting the balancing stepsize alpha_T^* into the expansion gives m_T=O(T^{-1/2}), and choose a T^{-1}-near minimizer.

If a subsequence has alpha_tilde_T bounded below by delta, condition before the current noise draw. The arithmetic average receives -(alpha/n) one^T epsilon_t, so conditional independence and exact variance sigma^2 force a positive variance lower bound and contradict m_T=O(T^{-1/2}).

If a subsequence has alpha_tilde_T T bounded by M, the slow multiplier lower bound from (8.3) keeps the mean slow mode at a fixed positive proportion over the horizon; after removing finitely many initial periods, Jensen gives a positive lower bound on J_T, again contradicting the near-minimal O(T^{-1/2}) value.

proof.description: Now every near-minimizing sequence lies in the uniform region of (8.8). Define the two-term leading expression s_T for that sequence.
Use the uniform expansion to get J_T(alpha_tilde_T)=s_T+o(s_T); since the near-minimal value is O(T^{-1/2}), s_T is O(T^{-1/2}). AM--GM gives the lower bound with h^2/q rewritten as n_eff.
Substituting alpha_T^* into the same expansion gives the matching upper direction for the infimum, and the two directions combine into (8.1).

key_lemmas.statement_math: \text{固定任意可容许周期网络。取 }f_i(x)=\lambda x^2/2\text{，其中 }0<\lambda\le L\text{，并令所有节点和时刻的加性噪声 iid、均值为零且方差恰为 }\sigma^2>0\text{。则对运行期间保持常数的确定性步长，}\quad \inf_{\alpha_T\ge0}\frac1T\sum_{t<T}\E|\nabla f(\bar x_t)|^2=\sigma\sqrt{\frac{2\lambda\Delta}{\neff T}}+o(T^{-1/2}).
key_lemmas.role: Shows that the n_eff factor in the upper bound is sharp and supports the corollary characterizing n-fold speedup.

proof.description: Write w_t=Y_t-G_t and lift one period of the linear quadratic system.
At alpha=0 the lifted system has one simple unit eigenvalue in the consensus direction and all other spectrum strictly inside the unit disk; define the Riesz projection and stable part.

Let c_r=b_r^T 1. From nu-rec at alpha=0, identify the slow multiplier and phase noise coefficient.

proof.description: Define the scalar comparison process using the slow coefficients.
Use stable-power, analytic O(alpha^2) multiplier/noise errors, Duhamel expansion, and martingale orthogonality to compare the true average with u_t.
For the scalar process, define the single-period multiplier and expand it to first order.
Sum the bias geometric series and the steady-state noise geometric series; each period contributes alpha^2 sigma^2 p q+O(alpha^3) noise variance.
When alpha->0 and alpha T->infty, combine the scalar expansion with x_0^2=2 Delta/lambda and the comparison-error transfer to get lower-expansion.
The transfer from comparison-error uses the printed MT/UT inequality and the bound UT=O((alpha T)^{-1}+alpha).

Plug alpha_T^*=sqrt(2 Delta/(lambda sigma^2 q T)) into lower-expansion to show the optimum is at most O(T^{-1/2}); then any T^{-1}-near minimizer cannot have a subsequential nonzero alpha because fresh noise gives a fixed variance lower bound.

If alpha_tilde_T T is bounded, the slow multiplier keeps the mean slow mode at a positive proportion over the horizon while stable output is O(alpha_tilde_T), giving another contradiction. Hence lower-expansion applies uniformly to near minimizers.

key_lemmas.name: TrueNfoldSpeedupCriterion
key_lemmas.statement_math: \text{考虑一族网络与问题，使 }L,\Delta,\sigma\text{ 以及 }(7.11)\text{ 中的瞬态量一致有界，并令 }T/n\to\infty\text{。则主导随机项具有中心化 SGD 意义下的 }n\text{ 倍轮复杂度加速，当且仅当}\quad \neff=\Theta(n).

proof.description: Conversely, take lambda=L in the matching lower bound. A uniform O(1/sqrt(nT)) leading rate forces neff=Omega(n); since always neff<=n, this is equivalent to neff=Theta(n).
